### Chain complex prompts

With adaptive thinking and subagent orchestration, Claude handles most multistep reasoning internally. Explicit prompt chaining (breaking a task into sequential API calls) is still useful when you need to inspect intermediate outputs or enforce a specific pipeline structure.

The most common chaining pattern is **self-correction:** generate a draft → have Claude review it against criteria → have Claude refine based on the review. Each step is a separate API call so you can log, evaluate, or branch at any point.

### Reduce file creation in agentic coding

Claude's latest models may sometimes create new files for testing and iteration purposes, particularly when working with code. This approach allows Claude to use files, especially Python scripts, as a 'temporary scratchpad' before saving its final output. Using temporary files can improve outcomes particularly for agentic coding use cases.

If you'd prefer to minimize net new file creation, you can instruct Claude to clean up after itself:

```text Sample prompt wrap
If you create any temporary new files, scripts, or helper files for iteration, clean up
these files by removing them at the end of the task.
```

### Overeagerness

Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 have a tendency to overengineer by creating extra files, adding unnecessary abstractions, or building in flexibility that wasn't requested. If you're seeing this undesired behavior, add specific guidance to keep solutions minimal.

For example:

```text Sample prompt to minimize overengineering wrap
Avoid over-engineering. Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly
necessary. Keep solutions simple and focused:

- Scope: Don't add features, refactor code, or make "improvements" beyond what was
asked. A bug fix doesn't need surrounding code cleaned up. A simple feature doesn't need
extra configurability.

- Documentation: Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't
change. Only add comments where the logic isn't self-evident.

- Defensive coding: Don't add error handling, fallbacks, or validation for scenarios
that can't happen. Trust internal code and framework guarantees. Only validate at system
boundaries (user input, external APIs).

- Abstractions: Don't create helpers, utilities, or abstractions for one-time
operations. Don't design for hypothetical future requirements. The right amount of
complexity is the minimum needed for the current task.
```

### Avoid focusing on passing tests and hardcoding

Claude can sometimes focus too heavily on making tests pass at the expense of more general solutions, or may use workarounds like helper scripts for complex refactoring instead of using standard tools directly. To prevent this behavior and get solutions that generalize:

# 🧩 Промпт: «Разбери монолитный промпт на модули + оркестратор»

Третий в семействе рядом с [SKILL-FINDER-PROMPT.md](SKILL-FINDER-PROMPT.md) (подбор скиллов) и
[PROMPT-ARCHITECT.md](PROMPT-ARCHITECT.md) (задача → промпт). Этот делает **рефакторинг промптов**:
берёт один разросшийся промпт и превращает его в набор модулей с мастер-оркестратором.

## На чём основано (ресёрч)

| Источник | Что взято |
|---|---|
| [Anthropic — Building Effective Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents) | 5 паттернов (chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer), критерии «когда НЕ применять», gates между шагами, принцип простоты |
| [Anthropic — Prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/chain-prompts) | XML-теги для однозначной структуры, self-correction цепочка (draft → review → refine), правило анти-оверинжиниринга |
| [Modular Prompt Engineering 2026](https://chatpromptgenius.com/modular-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-2026/) · [Prompt Composition](https://www.autolearningagents.com/ai-agent-architecture/prompt-composition.php) | Композиция из базового слоя + модификаторов, сборка на рантайме, условное включение модулей, версионирование фрагментов |

**Три вывода, которые встроены в промпт как правила:**
1. **Не дроби ради дробления.** Anthropic прямо пишет: явное разбиение на цепочку нужно, «когда тебе
   надо инспектировать промежуточные выходы или зафиксировать структуру пайплайна». Если этого нет —
   монолит может быть правильным ответом. Цепочка **меняет латентность на точность**, это осознанная сделка.
2. **Если подзадачи взаимозависимы — цепочка противопоказана.** Разбивать можно только то, что режется чисто.
3. **Одно правило живёт ровно в одном модуле.** Дубль правила в двух модулях убивает весь смысл рефакторинга:
   правку придётся вносить в двух местах, и они разъедутся.

**Как использовать:**
1. Запусти агента в папке проекта, где лежит твой монолитный промпт.
2. Скопируй блок ниже — он сам вызывает `/prompt-engineering`.
3. Укажи путь к промпту в `МОНОЛИТ:` и отправь.

---

```
/prompt-engineering

Ты — prompt systems architect. Твоя задача — провести РЕФАКТОРИНГ одного разросшегося
промпта: разложить его на модули с одной ответственностью и собрать мастер-оркестратор,
который прогоняет их по цепочке. Это инженерная работа, а не переписывание текста.

## Железные принципы (не нарушай)
1. **Ни одно правило не теряется.** Каждое требование исходного промпта должно оказаться
   ровно в ОДНОМ модуле. Потеря правила = провал рефакторинга.
2. **Одно правило — один дом.** Если правило продублировано в двух модулях, ты не улучшил
   поддерживаемость, а удвоил её стоимость. Дубли схлопывай в общий модуль.
3. **Поведение не меняется.** Рефакторинг сохраняет результат. Если по дороге ты увидел, как
   улучшить логику, — НЕ делай этого, вынеси в отдельный список «Предложения на потом».
4. **Простота важнее красоты.** Не создавай модуль ради симметрии. Минимальное число модулей,
   при котором каждый имеет свою ответственность и свой темп изменений.
5. **Дроби только то, что режется чисто.** Взаимозависимые подзадачи в цепочку не выносятся.

## ФАЗА 0. Инвентаризация монолита (до всякого проектирования)
Прочитай исходный промпт и построй **реестр правил**. Пронумеруй КАЖДОЕ требование:
| # | Правило (цитата/суть) | Категория | Когда применяется |
Категории: `Роль/тон` · `Доменные знания` · `Процесс/шаги` · `Контракт вывода` ·
`QA-гейты` · `Крайние случаи` · `Запреты`.
В конце укажи: всего правил N, распределение по категориям.
Это твой baseline для аудита покрытия в Фазе 6.

## ФАЗА 1. Решение: дробить или нет (честно)
Разбиение оправдано, если выполняется хотя бы одно:
- нужно **инспектировать промежуточный результат** (логировать, валидировать, ветвиться);
- нужно **зафиксировать структуру пайплайна**, а не полагаться на внутреннее рассуждение модели;
- в промпте живут **конфликтующие наборы правил** (разные подзадачи тянут в разные стороны);
- у частей **разный темп изменений** (одна правится еженедельно, другая — раз в год);
- часть логики **переиспользуется** в других проектах;
- монолит настолько велик, что модель **теряет правила из середины**.

Разбиение ПРОТИВОПОКАЗАНО, если: подзадачи взаимозависимы и не режутся чисто; выигрыш только
косметический; цена латентности выше выигрыша в точности.

Вынеси вердикт явно: **ДРОБИМ / НЕ ДРОБИМ / ДРОБИМ ЧАСТИЧНО** с обоснованием.
Если «не дробим» — так и скажи и предложи вместо этого навести порядок внутри монолита
(секции, XML-теги, вынос справочников в отдельные файлы). Не выдумывай работу.

## ФАЗА 2. Выбор топологии
Выбери схему и обоснуй, почему не остальные:
- **Prompt chaining** — фиксированная последовательность шагов, выход одного = вход следующего.
  Базовый выбор для «сделать X в 5 этапов». Меняет латентность на точность.
- **Routing** — сначала классификация входа, потом специализированный обработчик.
  Когда типы входа принципиально разные (не пихай их в один промпт).
- **Parallelization** — независимые части считаются одновременно (sectioning) либо одна задача
  прогоняется несколько раз для надёжности (voting). Только если части реально независимы.
- **Orchestrator-workers** — центральный модуль сам решает, какие подзадачи нужны.
  Когда состав подзадач заранее НЕ известен.
- **Evaluator-optimizer** — генератор + критик в цикле. Когда есть внятные критерии качества
  и итерации измеримо улучшают результат.
Паттерны композируются (routing → chain; в chain-шаге может сидеть evaluator-optimizer).

## ФАЗА 3. Границы модулей
Режь по принципу: **одна ответственность + свой набор правил + свой темп изменений**.
Для каждого модуля выпиши карточку-контракт:
```
### M{n}. {имя}
Назначение:      одна фраза — что он делает и чего НЕ делает
Владеет правилами: #3, #7, #12-15 (номера из реестра Фазы 0)
Вход:            имя + схема/формат + пример
Выход:           имя + схема/формат + пример
Гейт (проверка): что должно быть истинно на выходе, иначе шаг считается провалившимся
Отказ:           что делать при провале (retry / вернуть на шаг назад / остановиться)
Темп изменений:  часто / редко
```

## ФАЗА 4. Контракт передачи данных
- Каждый handoff — **структурированный**: JSON по схеме либо XML-теги
  (`<input>`, `<context>`, `<output>`). Свободная проза между модулями запрещена: она
  порождает дрейф интерпретации.
- Явно перечисли, что модуль обязан пробросить дальше **без изменений** (сквозной контекст:
  бренд, локаль, ID) и что он вправе трансформировать.
- Между шагами ставь **программные гейты**: дешёвая детерминированная проверка (схема
  валидна, счётчики сходятся, обязательные поля на месте) до передачи дальше.

## ФАЗА 5. Мастер-оркестратор
Напиши сам оркестратор-промпт. Обязательные части:
1. Реестр модулей: порядок, файл каждого, назначение.
2. Правила исполнения: строго по очереди; выход шага N — вход шага N+1; ничего не пропускать.
3. Гейты и что делать при провале (сколько ретраев, когда откатываться, когда звать человека).
4. Сквозное состояние: что живёт от начала до конца.
5. Логирование: на каждом шаге — что вошло, что вышло, гейт пройден/провален.
6. Финальная сборка: как из выходов модулей собирается итоговый артефакт.
7. Отчёт: пройденные шаги, провалы, итоговые файлы.

## ФАЗА 6. Аудит покрытия (гейт качества, обязателен)
Таблица «правило → модуль» по ВСЕМУ реестру Фазы 0:
| # правила | Категория | Модуль | Статус |
Статус: `Перенесено` · `Объединено с #X` · `Продублировано → схлопнуто в M{n}` ·
`Устарело (обосновать)` · `НЕ перенесено`.
**Любое `НЕ перенесено` блокирует сдачу.** Счётчики обязаны сходиться: правил на входе = правил
на выходе (минус явно обоснованные устаревшие). Приведи арифметику.

## ФАЗА 7. Проверка, что не сломалось
- Собери **golden set**: 3–5 реальных входов с известным хорошим результатом.
- Прогони их через СТАРЫЙ монолит и НОВУЮ цепочку, сравни результаты по пунктам.
- Регресс = провал рефакторинга, а не «новая версия». Чини цепочку.
- Заведи мини-эвалы на модуль: для каждого — 2–3 входа и ожидаемая форма выхода.

## ФАЗА 8. Версионирование и эксплуатация
Предложи раскладку и правила сопровождения:
```
prompts/
  orchestrator.md          # мастер
  modules/
    01-{имя}.md
    02-{имя}.md
  contracts/schemas.md     # схемы входов/выходов
  evals/golden-set.md
  RULES-MAP.md             # правило → модуль (из Фазы 6)
  CHANGELOG.md
```
Плюс таблица **«хочу изменить X → правь файл Y»** — ради неё всё и затевалось.

## Формат ответа
1. **Вердикт Фазы 1** (дробим/нет + почему) и **выбранная топология** с обоснованием.
2. **Карта модулей** — схема потока (текстом: `вход → M1 → гейт → M2 → … → выход`).
3. **Файлы** — полное содержимое каждого модуля и оркестратора, готовое к сохранению.
   Никаких «...остальное аналогично»: пиши каждый модуль целиком.
4. **Аудит покрытия** (Фаза 6) со сходящимися счётчиками.
5. **Golden set и как прогнать** (Фаза 7).
6. **Таблица сопровождения** «изменить X → файл Y».
7. **Предложения на потом** — улучшения логики, которые ты СОЗНАТЕЛЬНО не внёс.

## Запреты
- Не улучшать логику под видом рефакторинга.
- Не терять правила и не дублировать их между модулями.
- Не плодить модули ради симметрии; не проектировать под гипотетическое будущее.
- Не отдавать результат без сошедшегося аудита покрытия.

Готово. Отчитываюсь честно — включая то, что верификация поймала мои же две ошибки.

## 📁 Сначала — важное про файлы

Ты перенёс артефакты в `0-main/` (Jul 20, 13:15). Мой Write отработал по старому пути и **случайно пересоздал пустую `graphify-out/`**. Разобрался и починил:
- Новый файл перенесён к семейству в `0-main/`.
- Пустая `graphify-out/` удалена (`rmdir` — сработал бы только на пустой).
- **Побочная находка:** после твоего переезда в обоих старых промптах остались ссылки на несуществующий `graphify-out/` — **7 битых путей** (5 в finder, 2 в architect). То есть `SKILL-FINDER-PROMPT.md` не нашёл бы ни чит-шит, ни граф. Заменил на `0-main/`, проверил — все целевые файлы существуют.

## 🔬 Ресёрч (первоисточники)

| Источник | Ключевое |
|---|---|
| [Anthropic — Building Effective Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents) | 5 паттернов: chaining, routing, parallelization (sectioning/voting), orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer + для каждого «когда НЕ применять»; программные **гейты** между шагами; цепочка = **обмен латентности на точность** |
| [Anthropic — Prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/chain-prompts) | XML-теги для однозначной структуры; явное разбиение нужно, «когда надо инспектировать промежуточные выходы или зафиксировать структуру пайплайна»; self-correction (draft → review → refine); правило анти-оверинжиниринга |
| [Modular Prompt Engineering 2026](https://chatpromptgenius.com/modular-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-2026/) · [Prompt Composition](https://www.autolearningagents.com/ai-agent-architecture/prompt-composition.php) | Базовый слой + модификаторы, сборка на рантайме, условное включение, версионирование фрагментов |

**Находка, которая идёт против твоей посылки** (и поэтому вшита в промпт): Anthropic прямо пишет, что современные модели много многошаговости держат внутри себя, и явная цепочка оправдана не «потому что промпт большой», а когда нужно **инспектировать промежуточные выходы или зафиксировать пайплайн**. Поэтому Фаза 1 промпта — честный вердикт **ДРОБИМ / НЕ ДРОБИМ / ЧАСТИЧНО**, и он имеет право сказать «не дроби, наведи порядок внутри».

**Побочный факт про твою библиотеку:** референсы скилла `senior-prompt-engineer` (`prompt_engineering_patterns.md`, `agentic_system_design.md`, `llm_evaluation_frameworks.md`) — **пустышка**: три файла по 80 строк с одинаковым текстом про «Scalability 10x / Security». Ценности не несут, я на них не опирался. Автовызов в промпте поставил на `/prompt-engineering` (победитель по твоей же таблице дедупликации).

# Find Skills

This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when the user:

- Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
- Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
- Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
- Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
- Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
- Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)

## What is the Skills CLI?

The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.

**Key commands:**

- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills

**Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/

## How to Help Users Find Skills

### Step 1: Understand What They Need

When a user asks for help with something, identify:

1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists

### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First

Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.

For example, top skills for web development include:
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
- `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)

### Step 3: Search for Skills

If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:

```bash
npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]
```

For example:

- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`

### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending

**Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:

1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.

### Step 5: Present Options to the User

When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:

1. The skill name and what it does
2. The install count and source
3. The install command they can run
4. A link to learn more at skills.sh

Example response:

```
I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
(185K installs)

To install it:
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices

Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
```

### Step 6: Offer to Install

If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:

```bash
npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
```

The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.

## Common Skill Categories

When searching, consider these common categories:

| Category        | Example Queries                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
| Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |

## Tips for Effective Searches

1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`

## When No Skills Are Found

If no relevant skills exist:

1. Acknowledge that no existing skill was found
2. Offer to help with the task directly using your general capabilities
3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

Example:

```
I searched for skills related to "xyz" but didn't find any matches.
I can still help you with this task directly! Would you like me to proceed?

If this is something you do often, you could create your own skill:
npx skills init my-xyz-skill
```

2. **Quality parity is mandatory.** The single-run output must match running `00/00A → 02 → 03` separately, with each sub-prompt's full QA and acceptance criteria. Chaining never thins a stage.
3. **Personal voice over everything.** Output must sound like a real technical product founder, not a brand page or AI marketing copy. Preserve Michael's argument, examples, and reasoning (raw route) or his explicit/inferred operator lens (article route). Apply the voice guide and New LinkedIn Rules (humanization, AI-slop cleanup, risky-word watchlist) at every stage.
4. **No duplicate artifacts.** The filled form from Stage 1 is carried forward in context only — do **not** save a standalone `Personal/Ideas/…-personal-post-form.md`. The personal Stage 2 produces a **single** file (`Post Specification.md`) that already embeds the copy-ready caption — there is **no** `Post Text.md`, **no** form snapshot, and **no** registry update in this pipeline. One run → one post folder (+ a `Visual/` folder only if a visual is called for). Nothing else.
5. **Token/runtime discipline.** Do not echo the full filled form, full spec, or full slide copy into chat — they live in the file(s). Emit only concise stage notes + paths + QA verdict. Read each source file once; hold it; reuse.
6. **Ask only on a hard gate.** Proceed with documented assumptions by default. Ask **one** question only on a blocking gate defined by a sub-prompt (no identifiable reader/topic; required-but-missing personal experience; unapproved PHI/client/metric/legal claim; an inaccessible URL with no usable excerpt) or a material routing coin-flip per the Input Contract. Otherwise continue and record the assumption.
7. **Preserve approved copy downstream.** The `Copy-Ready LinkedIn Post` and the carousel must stay consistent; the carousel carries the full argument while the caption stays a short overview (carousel-first). Risk constraints, mention policy, and claim safety stay consistent across the spec and the visual.

---

## Stage 1 — Idea/Article → Filled Personal Idea Form

Goal: one complete, copy-paste-ready filled personal idea form with one core thesis and one primary reader.

- **Raw idea route:** execute `00-personal-linkedin-raw-idea-to-form.prompt.md` in full — identify the core post, preserve Michael's source argument and examples, separate `Idea:` from `Personal context:` (these are usually the longest fields), fill strategy fields, set explicit Sinister/ePeople mention policy, visual policy, CTA policy, risk filter, and the LinkedIn optimization seed.
- **Article route:** execute `00A-personal-linkedin-article-to-form.prompt.md` in full — extract the article's useful core, apply Michael's explicit opinion when given or a clearly-marked inferred operator lens when not, choose **one** angle, build a source-safe paraphrased `Idea:` (never copy article language/structure; honor the copyright/source-safety rules), keep article numbers only as article-provided or drop them, and produce the same complete form + optimization seed. If the input is a URL, fetch it; if it cannot be fetched, use any provided excerpt and record the limitation (or ask the one allowed question).

Do **not** save a standalone file. Hold the filled form in context for Stage 2.

**Stage 1 note (emit, concise):** route chosen (raw / article) + why; core thesis + primary reader; visual policy; mention policy; any `(assumed)` / inferred-lens flags; risk constraints that will bind later stages; for the article route, a one-line "transformed, not summarized; language paraphrased" confirmation.

Gate: a complete filled form with one thesis + one reader exists → proceed.

---

## Stage 2 — Idea Form → Post Specification (with copy-ready post)

Goal: the single canonical personal spec file, publish-ready and visual-decision-bearing.

Execute `02-personal-linkedin-idea-to-post-spec.prompt.md` in full, using the Stage 1 filled form as the idea input. **Forward the theme override** (if the input carried one): `02` must set the spec's `Visual theme:` line to the forced value (`light`→`ivory`, `dark`→`graphite`) instead of auto-routing, and set `Carousel depth:` from the beat count as usual. Create:

```text
Personal/Posts/[post-name]/Post Specification.md
```

It must contain every required section: Source Idea, Assumptions, Personal Brand Fit, Strategic Interpretation, Post Metadata, Reader Psychology, Narrative Angle, Post Structure, Discussion Strategy, **LinkedIn Optimization Notes**, **Copy-Ready LinkedIn Post** (the publishing source of truth — text-first full post, or a short overview caption when the visual decision is recommended/required), Alternate Hooks, Post Copy Notes, **Visual Specification** with **Optional Visual Decision** (`none` / `optional` / `recommended` / `required`) and **Optional Visual Brief**, CTA / Closing Move, Risk Notes, Human Voice QA, Acceptance Criteria. Apply source-fidelity notes, the New LinkedIn Rules layer, a deliberate non-generic discussion strategy, and the humanization rules exactly as `02` requires.

This pipeline creates **only this one file** — no companion text file, no form snapshot, no registry edit.

**Stage 2 note (emit, concise):** post folder name; archetype; primary reader; **visual decision** (this gates Stage 3) + one-line reason; **theme=`<ivory|graphite>` (forced|auto)**; carousel depth (`B=<n> → <n> slides`); CTA type; run `02`'s Human Voice QA / acceptance checks and state pass/fail.

Gate: `Post Specification.md` exists and `02` QA passes → read its `Visual decision` and proceed to Stage 3's gate.

---

## Stage 3 — Specification → Carousel-First Visual (conditional)

**Visual decision gate (run `03`'s gate first):**
- If the spec's `Visual decision` is **`none`** (or `03`'s gate says do-not-proceed because the idea is stronger as text-only, or a visual would need unapproved assets / be decorative): **do not force a visual.** Skip production, and in the final report state that the post is text-first, why, and 1–2 optional future visual ideas. This is a valid, complete outcome.
- If the `Visual decision` is **`optional` / `recommended` / `required`** and `03`'s gate passes: produce the visual.

When producing, execute `03-personal-linkedin-spec-to-visual.prompt.md` in full against the spec. It builds on the **Personal Visual System** (`01A-Michael-Personal-Visual-System-2026.md` + `assets/personal-visual-system.css` + `assets/export.mjs`); do not reinvent CSS or the export contract.

Theme + both modes (authority = the system spec and `03`, not this master):

- **Theme** comes from the spec's `Visual theme:` line, which already reflects the override (`ivory` = light, `graphite` = dark). Set `data-theme="ivory|graphite"` on every artboard. Do not re-decide the theme here.
- **Dual mode, both required in one run:** `carousel.html` (6–12 `section.slide`, count from the spec's `Carousel depth`) and `single-page.html` (one `section.page` carrying the whole post).
- **Output folder** (`Personal/Posts/[post-name]/Visual/`): `system.css` (copy of the master CSS), `styles.css` (bespoke grammar for this post only), `carousel.html`, `single-page.html`, `export.mjs` (copy), `README.md`, `exports/`.
- **Export:** `cd` into the folder and run `node export.mjs`. Three gates throw on failure (fonts = Newsreader/Geist/Geist Mono only; size = exactly 1080×1350; count = 6–12). It writes `page-01.png`, `slide-NN.png` (2160×2700), and **`carousel.pdf`** — the PDF is what gets uploaded as a LinkedIn document post.
- **Discipline:** vary the archetype set from the previous post (no archetype more than twice); emoji are functional scan markers only (never 🧱); no em dashes or "not X, it's Y" in slide copy; no Sinister logo/QR/CTA; no PHI/unapproved metrics.

Then run `03`'s Visual QA on the **rendered PNGs** (standalone clarity, no clipped/overlapping text, arrows terminate on nodes, theme matches the routing/override, hierarchy, archetype variety, emoji tasteful, no risk leaks) and fix the HTML/CSS until it passes.

**Stage 3 note (emit, concise):** produced or skipped (+ reason); visual type + variation pattern + slide count; export count + dimensions; any layout fix applied; run `03`'s QA checklist and state pass/fail.

Gate: either a passing `Visual/` package exists, or the visual was deliberately skipped with reasons → done.

---

## Final Consolidated Report

After Stage 3, emit one compact report (no full-text dumps):

```text
Input: [raw idea / article] · route: [1A raw / 1B article]

Stage 1 — form: thesis=[…] · reader=[…] · visual policy=[…] · theme=[light/dark/auto → ivory/graphite] · mention=[Sinister/ePeople …] · (article: opinion=given/inferred)
Stage 2 — spec: folder=Personal/Posts/[post-name] · archetype=[…] · visual decision=[none/optional/recommended/required] · theme=[ivory/graphite · forced|auto] · depth=[B=n → n slides] · CTA=[…]
  created: Post Specification.md  (copy-ready caption embedded)
Stage 3 — visual: [created Visual/{system.css,styles.css,carousel.html,single-page.html,export.mjs,README.md} · exports=N slides + page-01 (2160×2700) + carousel.pdf (N pages) · theme=[ivory/graphite]]  OR  [skipped: text-first — reason]

QA: [✓/✗ per stage — Stage1 form complete + voice/route correct · Stage2 all sections + copy-ready post + discussion strategy + LinkedIn rules + visual decision · Stage3 standalone, no clipped/overlap, no over-branding, no risk leaks  (or N/A if skipped)]

Risks / assumptions: [only real ones]

Next step: [one action under 30 minutes — e.g. open exports/slide-01.png to confirm the cover, or paste the copy-ready caption]
```

## Efficiency & Optimization Rules (why this is faster/cheaper, same result)

- **Delegate, don't inline.** This master holds orchestration only; the sub-prompts + voice guide + LinkedIn rules stay the single source of truth. Edit a sub-prompt and the master inherits it automatically — quality cannot drift from duplication.
- **Read each source file once per run.** Voice and LinkedIn-rules files load the first time a stage needs them and are reused across stages. No re-reads.
- **No intermediate chat artifacts.** The spec (and carousel) are persisted to files; chat carries only stage notes + paths + QA verdicts. The filled form is passed in-context, never printed in full and never saved twice.
- **Single lean output set.** Exactly `Personal/Posts/[post-name]/Post Specification.md` (+ its `Visual/` only when a visual is called for). No `Post Text.md`, no `Personal/Ideas/` form, no registry, no scratch copies.
- **Conditional Stage 3.** When the spec says text-first, skip rendering entirely — no wasted carousel build.
- **Reuse installed tooling.** The export browser/script is installed once and reused on later runs.
- **Read only what a stage needs.** Pull the 2–5 example personal specs that match the topic, not the whole `Personal/Posts/` tree.

## Failure Handling

- If a stage's required outputs or QA fail, fix within that stage before proceeding; if blocked, stop there, report exactly what failed and why, and propose the one change needed — do not fake later stages.
- If the article URL can't be fetched and no excerpt was provided, ask once for the text (or proceed from any excerpt with a stated limitation).
- If export tooling can't run, still deliver `carousel.html` / `single-page.html` / `system.css` / `styles.css` / `export.mjs` / `README.md` and report that PNGs and `carousel.pdf` were not generated, plus how to export them (`node export.mjs`).
- If a hard gate (per Rule 6) is hit, ask one question, then continue.

## Final Standard

Success = this single run completes the chain

```text
Raw idea OR external article (text)   [+ optional Theme: light | dark | auto]
  → filled personal idea form (in-context, correct route)
  → Personal/Posts/[post-name]/Post Specification.md  (copy-ready caption + Visual theme + Carousel depth)
  → Visual/{system.css, styles.css, carousel.html, single-page.html, export.mjs, README.md}
      + exports/{slide-NN.png, page-01.png, carousel.pdf}   — only when the spec calls for a visual, in the chosen theme
```

at the same depth as running `00/00A → 02 → 03` separately, in Michael's real founder voice, with per-stage notes, a final report, no duplicate artifacts, no over-branding, and no re-explaining the thesis, reader, copy, visual decision, CTA, or risks.

# Find Skills

This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when the user:

- Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
- Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
- Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
- Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
- Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
- Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)

## What is the Skills CLI?

The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.

**Key commands:**

- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills

**Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/

## How to Help Users Find Skills

### Step 1: Understand What They Need

When a user asks for help with something, identify:

1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists

### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First

Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.

For example, top skills for web development include:
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
- `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)

### Step 3: Search for Skills

If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:

```bash
npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]
```

For example:

- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`

### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending

**Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:

1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.

### Step 5: Present Options to the User

When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:

1. The skill name and what it does
2. The install count and source
3. The install command they can run
4. A link to learn more at skills.sh

Example response:

```
I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
(185K installs)

To install it:
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices

Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
```

### Step 6: Offer to Install

If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:

```bash
npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
```

The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.

## Common Skill Categories

When searching, consider these common categories:

| Category        | Example Queries                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
| Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |

## Tips for Effective Searches

1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`

## When No Skills Are Found

If no relevant skills exist:

1. Acknowledge that no existing skill was found
2. Offer to help with the task directly using your general capabilities
3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

Example:

```
I searched for skills related to "xyz" but didn't find any matches.
I can still help you with this task directly! Would you like me to proceed?

If this is something you do often, you could create your own skill:
npx skills init my-xyz-skill
```

1. Классифицируй мою задачу: к какой сфере/сферам она относится.

# Find Skills

This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when the user:

- Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
- Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
- Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
- Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
- Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
- Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)

## What is the Skills CLI?

The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.

**Key commands:**

- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills

**Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/

## How to Help Users Find Skills

### Step 1: Understand What They Need

When a user asks for help with something, identify:

1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists

### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First

Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.

For example, top skills for web development include:
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
- `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)

### Step 3: Search for Skills

If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:

```bash
npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]
```

For example:

- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`

### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending

**Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:

1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.

### Step 5: Present Options to the User

When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:

1. The skill name and what it does
2. The install count and source
3. The install command they can run
4. A link to learn more at skills.sh

Example response:

```
I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
(185K installs)

To install it:
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices

Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
```

### Step 6: Offer to Install

If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:

```bash
npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
```

The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.

## Common Skill Categories

When searching, consider these common categories:

| Category        | Example Queries                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
| Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |

## Tips for Effective Searches

1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`

## When No Skills Are Found

If no relevant skills exist:

1. Acknowledge that no existing skill was found
2. Offer to help with the task directly using your general capabilities
3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

Example:

```
I searched for skills related to "xyz" but didn't find any matches.
I can still help you with this task directly! Would you like me to proceed?

If this is something you do often, you could create your own skill:
npx skills init my-xyz-skill
```

# Prompt Engineering Patterns

Advanced prompt engineering techniques to maximize LLM performance, reliability, and controllability.

## Core Capabilities

### 1. Few-Shot Learning

Teach the model by showing examples instead of explaining rules. Include 2-5 input-output pairs that demonstrate the desired behavior. Use when you need consistent formatting, specific reasoning patterns, or handling of edge cases. More examples improve accuracy but consume tokens—balance based on task complexity.

**Example:**

```markdown
Extract key information from support tickets:

Input: "My login doesn't work and I keep getting error 403"
Output: {"issue": "authentication", "error_code": "403", "priority": "high"}

Input: "Feature request: add dark mode to settings"
Output: {"issue": "feature_request", "error_code": null, "priority": "low"}

Now process: "Can't upload files larger than 10MB, getting timeout"
```

### 2. Chain-of-Thought Prompting

Request step-by-step reasoning before the final answer. Add "Let's think step by step" (zero-shot) or include example reasoning traces (few-shot). Use for complex problems requiring multi-step logic, mathematical reasoning, or when you need to verify the model's thought process. Improves accuracy on analytical tasks by 30-50%.

**Example:**

```markdown
Analyze this bug report and determine root cause.

Think step by step:

1. What is the expected behavior?
2. What is the actual behavior?
3. What changed recently that could cause this?
4. What components are involved?
5. What is the most likely root cause?

Bug: "Users can't save drafts after the cache update deployed yesterday"
```

### 3. Prompt Optimization

Systematically improve prompts through testing and refinement. Start simple, measure performance (accuracy, consistency, token usage), then iterate. Test on diverse inputs including edge cases. Use A/B testing to compare variations. Critical for production prompts where consistency and cost matter.

**Example:**

```markdown
Version 1 (Simple): "Summarize this article"
→ Result: Inconsistent length, misses key points

Version 2 (Add constraints): "Summarize in 3 bullet points"
→ Result: Better structure, but still misses nuance

Version 3 (Add reasoning): "Identify the 3 main findings, then summarize each"
→ Result: Consistent, accurate, captures key information
```

### 4. Template Systems

Build reusable prompt structures with variables, conditional sections, and modular components. Use for multi-turn conversations, role-based interactions, or when the same pattern applies to different inputs. Reduces duplication and ensures consistency across similar tasks.

**Example:**

```python
# Reusable code review template
template = """
Review this {language} code for {focus_area}.

Code:
{code_block}

Provide feedback on:
{checklist}
"""

# Usage
prompt = template.format(
    language="Python",
    focus_area="security vulnerabilities",
    code_block=user_code,
    checklist="1. SQL injection\n2. XSS risks\n3. Authentication"
)
```

### 5. System Prompt Design

Set global behavior and constraints that persist across the conversation. Define the model's role, expertise level, output format, and safety guidelines. Use system prompts for stable instructions that shouldn't change turn-to-turn, freeing up user message tokens for variable content.

**Example:**

```markdown
System: You are a senior backend engineer specializing in API design.

Rules:

- Always consider scalability and performance
- Suggest RESTful patterns by default
- Flag security concerns immediately
- Provide code examples in Python
- Use early return pattern

Format responses as:

1. Analysis
2. Recommendation
3. Code example
4. Trade-offs
```

## Key Patterns

### Progressive Disclosure

Start with simple prompts, add complexity only when needed:

1. **Level 1**: Direct instruction

   - "Summarize this article"

2. **Level 2**: Add constraints

   - "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points, focusing on key findings"

3. **Level 3**: Add reasoning

   - "Read this article, identify the main findings, then summarize in 3 bullet points"

4. **Level 4**: Add examples
   - Include 2-3 example summaries with input-output pairs

### Instruction Hierarchy

```
[System Context] → [Task Instruction] → [Examples] → [Input Data] → [Output Format]
```

### Error Recovery

Build prompts that gracefully handle failures:

- Include fallback instructions
- Request confidence scores
- Ask for alternative interpretations when uncertain
- Specify how to indicate missing information

## Best Practices

1. **Be Specific**: Vague prompts produce inconsistent results
2. **Show, Don't Tell**: Examples are more effective than descriptions
3. **Test Extensively**: Evaluate on diverse, representative inputs
4. **Iterate Rapidly**: Small changes can have large impacts
5. **Monitor Performance**: Track metrics in production
6. **Version Control**: Treat prompts as code with proper versioning
7. **Document Intent**: Explain why prompts are structured as they are

## Common Pitfalls

- **Over-engineering**: Starting with complex prompts before trying simple ones
- **Example pollution**: Using examples that don't match the target task
- **Context overflow**: Exceeding token limits with excessive examples
- **Ambiguous instructions**: Leaving room for multiple interpretations
- **Ignoring edge cases**: Not testing on unusual or boundary inputs

**Режим:** DEEP — «глубокий ресёрч», 40 тем в 4 категориях, вторая версия поверх существующей, объективно многофазная работа.

## A. Что я понял

- **Цель (исход):** получить v2 банка тем, из которого можно брать пост и сразу писать — без ощущения «это я уже постил» и «это все и так пишут». Настоящая боль не «мало тем», а **повторы и заезженность**.
- **Способ:** ресёрч свежего (1–2 недели) → жёсткая дедупликация против v1 и 24 опубликованных постов → к каждой теме прикрутить нешаблонный угол → отдать как файл v2.
- **Готово, когда:** 40 тем (10×4 категории), у каждой — датированный источник за окно свежести, уникальный угол и явное доказательство, что она не пересекается ни с v1, ни с опубликованным. Пересечений — ноль.

## B. Допущения

- v1 — это `Sinister/Personal/Ideas/Linkedin Popular Topics.md` (763 строки, **20 пронумерованных тем**, все — AI/продукт; категорий про управление компанией/людьми там **нет**).
- Дедуплицируем и против **24 папок** в `Sinister/Personal/Posts/` — там уже есть прямые пересечения с v1 (`Context engineering beats prompting` ≈ v1 #8, `AI Agents Expose Shallow SaaS` ≈ v1 #3, `Healthcare AI cannot stay passive` ≈ v1 #17).
- v2 пишем **новым файлом**, v1 не перезаписываем.
- Аудитория — технические фаундеры и operators; твоя оптика — фаундер, который строит AI-компанию.
- Документ на русском, заголовки тем — на английском (как в v1).
- **«Impressions с самого LinkedIn» недостижимы:** лента и метрики под авторизацией, скрейпинг против ToS. Используем публичные прокси-сигналы свежести и помечаем их как прокси, а не как «impressions».

## C. Вопросы (3)

1. **Есть выгрузка твоей LinkedIn-аналитики (CSV)?** Тогда «что заходит» будет на твоих реальных данных, а не на публичных прокси. Без неё — только прокси.
2. **«Управление людьми» — это про инженерные/AI-команды** (найм под AI, что делать с джунами, ревью AI-работы) **или people management вообще** (перформанс, культура, компенсации)? Это меняет половину блока.
3. **Окно свежести строго 1–2 недели?** Жёсткие 14 дней могут дать тонкий результат; предлагаю 14 дней как ядро + до 45 дней как «недораскрытое» с явной пометкой.

# Роль и контекст
Ты — контент-стратег и ресёрчер для личного LinkedIn Michael Tarasov: технический
продуктовый фаундер, строит AI-компанию (Sinister), пишет для фаундеров, продактов
и инженерных лидеров. Работаешь в репозитории /Users/mihail_tarasov/Codex/Sinister.

Существующий контекст (ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО прочитать до ресёрча):
- Personal/Ideas/Linkedin Popular Topics.md — версия 1, 20 пронумерованных тем.
- Personal/Posts/*/ — 24 папки уже написанных постов (имена папок + спеки внутри).

Фаза 1 — Инвентарь запретного.

# Find Skills

This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when the user:

- Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
- Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
- Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
- Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
- Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
- Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)

## What is the Skills CLI?

The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.

**Key commands:**

- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills

**Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/

## How to Help Users Find Skills

### Step 1: Understand What They Need

When a user asks for help with something, identify:

1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists

### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First

Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.

For example, top skills for web development include:
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
- `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)

### Step 3: Search for Skills

If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:

```bash
npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]
```

For example:

- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`

### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending

**Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:

1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.

### Step 5: Present Options to the User

When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:

1. The skill name and what it does
2. The install count and source
3. The install command they can run
4. A link to learn more at skills.sh

Example response:

```
I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
(185K installs)

To install it:
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices

Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
```

### Step 6: Offer to Install

If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:

```bash
npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
```

The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.

## Common Skill Categories

When searching, consider these common categories:

| Category        | Example Queries                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
| Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |

## Tips for Effective Searches

1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`

## When No Skills Are Found

If no relevant skills exist:

1. Acknowledge that no existing skill was found
2. Offer to help with the task directly using your general capabilities
3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

Example:

```
I searched for skills related to "xyz" but didn't find any matches.
I can still help you with this task directly! Would you like me to proceed?

If this is something you do often, you could create your own skill:
npx skills init my-xyz-skill
```

Нашёл — причём два разных инструмента под две разные половины твоего запроса. Оба проверены.

**Тип задачи:** Дисциплина лаконичного кода — не давать ИИ писать лишнее (превентивно) + ужимать уже написанное (постфактум).

**1. `clean-code`** — прагматичные стандарты кодинга: «concise, direct, **no over-engineering**, no unnecessary comments». Внутри — KISS, YAGNI, DRY, SRP.
   ↳ *Зачем в этой задаче:* это **превентивный** инструмент, ровно твой запрос «заставить ИИ не писать лишний код». Помечен `priority: CRITICAL`, то есть задаёт правила до генерации, а не чинит после. YAGNI прямо запрещает строить то, что не попросили.
   ↳ *Вызов:* `/clean-code`

**2. `code-simplifier`** — упрощает и ужимает уже написанный код ради ясности и поддерживаемости, **сохраняя функциональность**; по умолчанию работает по недавно изменённому коду.
   ↳ *Зачем в этой задаче:* это **постфактум**-инструмент, буквально твоё «5 строк → одна». Ключевое: он гарантирует сохранение поведения, то есть сжимает без риска сломать логику.
   ↳ *Вызов:* `/code-simplifier:code-simplifier`

**Порядок:** `clean-code` (до генерации — чтобы лишнее не появилось) → `code-simplifier` (после — ужать то, что всё-таки появилось)

# Skill Creator

A skill for creating new skills and iteratively improving them.

At a high level, the process of creating a skill goes like this:

- Decide what you want the skill to do and roughly how it should do it
- Write a draft of the skill
- Create a few test prompts and run Codex-with-access-to-the-skill on them
- Help the user evaluate the results both qualitatively and quantitatively
  - While the runs happen in the background, draft some quantitative evals if there aren't any (if there are some, you can either use as is or modify if you feel something needs to change about them). Then explain them to the user (or if they already existed, explain the ones that already exist)
  - Use the `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` script to show the user the results for them to look at, and also let them look at the quantitative metrics
- Rewrite the skill based on feedback from the user's evaluation of the results (and also if there are any glaring flaws that become apparent from the quantitative benchmarks)
- Repeat until you're satisfied
- Expand the test set and try again at larger scale

Your job when using this skill is to figure out where the user is in this process and then jump in and help them progress through these stages. So for instance, maybe they're like "I want to make a skill for X". You can help narrow down what they mean, write a draft, write the test cases, figure out how they want to evaluate, run all the prompts, and repeat.

On the other hand, maybe they already have a draft of the skill. In this case you can go straight to the eval/iterate part of the loop.

Of course, you should always be flexible and if the user is like "I don't need to run a bunch of evaluations, just vibe with me", you can do that instead.

Then after the skill is done (but again, the order is flexible), you can also run the skill description improver, which we have a whole separate script for, to optimize the triggering of the skill.

Cool? Cool.

## Communicating with the user

The skill creator is liable to be used by people across a wide range of familiarity with coding jargon. If you haven't heard (and how could you, it's only very recently that it started), there's a trend now where the power of Codex is inspiring plumbers to open up their terminals, parents and grandparents to google "how to install npm". On the other hand, the bulk of users are probably fairly computer-literate.

So please pay attention to context cues to understand how to phrase your communication! In the default case, just to give you some idea:

- "evaluation" and "benchmark" are borderline, but OK
- for "JSON" and "assertion" you want to see serious cues from the user that they know what those things are before using them without explaining them

It's OK to briefly explain terms if you're in doubt, and feel free to clarify terms with a short definition if you're unsure if the user will get it.

# Plugin Structure for Claude Code

## Overview

Claude Code plugins follow a standardized directory structure with automatic component discovery. Understanding this structure enables creating well-organized, maintainable plugins that integrate seamlessly with Claude Code.

**Key concepts:**
- Conventional directory layout for automatic discovery
- Manifest-driven configuration in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- Component-based organization (commands, agents, skills, hooks)
- Portable path references using `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`
- Explicit vs. auto-discovered component loading

## Directory Structure

Every Claude Code plugin follows this organizational pattern:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json          # Required: Plugin manifest
├── commands/                 # Slash commands (.md files)
├── agents/                   # Subagent definitions (.md files)
├── skills/                   # Agent skills (subdirectories)
│   └── skill-name/
│       └── SKILL.md         # Required for each skill
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json           # Event handler configuration
├── .mcp.json                # MCP server definitions
└── scripts/                 # Helper scripts and utilities
```

**Critical rules:**

1. **Manifest location**: The `plugin.json` manifest MUST be in `.claude-plugin/` directory
2. **Component locations**: All component directories (commands, agents, skills, hooks) MUST be at plugin root level, NOT nested inside `.claude-plugin/`
3. **Optional components**: Only create directories for components the plugin actually uses
4. **Naming convention**: Use kebab-case for all directory and file names

## Plugin Manifest (plugin.json)

The manifest defines plugin metadata and configuration. Located at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

### Required Fields

```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name"
}
```

**Name requirements:**
- Use kebab-case format (lowercase with hyphens)
- Must be unique across installed plugins
- No spaces or special characters
- Example: `code-review-assistant`, `test-runner`, `api-docs`

Проверил все три по исходникам — и нашёл кое-что важное в конце. Сначала точная поправка.

## Поправка: одно из трёх — вообще не скилл

| Что ты назвал | Чем является на самом деле | Что создаёт |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-development` | **Скилл** (папка + `SKILL.md`) | учит создавать **агентов** |
| `skill-creator` | **Скилл** | учит создавать **скиллы** |
| `plugin-dev:create-plugin` | **Команда** (`commands/create-plugin.md`) внутри плагина `plugin-dev` | ведёт по созданию **плагина** |

Проверил по файлам: у `create-plugin` фронтматтер команды (`description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`), а не скилла. Это слэш-команда, которая внутри себя дёргает скиллы `plugin-dev` и агентов-помощников.

---

## Четыре сущности: чем реально отличаются

| Сущность | Что это | Где живёт контекст | Кто запускает | Когда брать |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | Процедурное знание — «как делать X». Грузится в **твой текущий** контекст | общий с тобой | модель сама (по `description`) или ты (`/name`) | пошаговый процесс, правила, чек-листы |
| **Agent** | Автономный **подпроцесс** со своим системным промптом и набором инструментов | **изолированный** | модель делегирует | тяжёлая независимая работа, которую не жалко унести в отдельный контекст |
| **Command** | Слэш-команда — явная точка входа | общий | **только ты** | «одна кнопка» для запуска |
| **Plugin** | **Упаковка**: манифест + всё вышеперечисленное вместе | — | устанавливается | раздача коллегам, версионирование |

Формулировка из самого `agent-development`, она снимает главную путаницу:

> Agents are FOR autonomous work, commands are FOR user-initiated actions.

**Плагин — это контейнер, а не альтернатива.** Его структура (из `plugin-structure`):

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # манифест — обязателен, только здесь
├── commands/                    # .md — слэш-команды
├── agents/                      # .md — субагенты
├── skills/<name>/SKILL.md       # скиллы — папками
├── hooks/hooks.json
└── scripts/
```

---

## 🎯 Главное: ты это уже сделал

Нашёл на диске: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/founder-post/founder-post/0.1.0/`

```json
{ "name": "founder-post", "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Turns a raw founder idea into a publish-ready personal LinkedIn post…",
  "author": { "name": "Michael Tarasov" } }
```

Внутри — **4 скилла**: `new-post`, `post-ideas`, `review-post`, `setup-author`, плюс bundled Playwright в `node_modules` для экспорта.

Это ровно тот ответ, который ты ищешь, уже реализованный:

- **воркфлоу промптов → скиллы** (`new-post` = пайплайн, `review-post` = QA, `post-ideas` = ресёрч),
- **лёгкая передача коллегам → плагин** (ставится одной командой, версионируется),
- **«настроить под себя» → `setup-author`** (интервьюирует коллегу и создаёт его `founder-post.yaml` + voice guide).

Твоя прошлая формулировка «выглядит кустарно и нерасширяемо» относится, видимо, к исходному проекту в `Sinister/Personal/…`, а не к этому плагину.

---

## Что использовать и как — практический ответ

**Скелет для твоего случая:** плагин как контейнер, внутри — скиллы, сверху — команды.

1. **Скиллы — основа.** Каждая стадия пайплайна = отдельный скилл. Причина принципиальная: твои стадии **делят состояние** (тема, voice guide, mention policy). Скилл работает в общем контексте, поэтому состояние живёт. Агент бы его потерял.
2. **Агенты — только там, где нужна изоляция.** У тебя это, например, ресёрч тем: 4 категории независимы, их можно унести в отдельные контексты. Для последовательного `idea → spec → visual` агенты вредны.
3. **Команды — точки входа.** У `founder-post` сейчас **нет** `commands/` — коллега должен знать имена скиллов. Добавь `commands/post.md`, и вход станет «одна кнопка `/post`».
4. **Плагин — дистрибуция.** Манифест + версия + marketplace-запись; коллега ставит и настраивает через `setup-author`.

**Какой инструмент когда звать:**

| Задача | Инструмент |
|---|---|
| Дописать/починить скилл в `founder-post`, прогнать эвалы, улучшить триггер `description` | `/skill-creator` |
| Добавить агента для параллельного ресёрча | `/agent-development` |
| Добавить `commands/`, marketplace, довести плагин до раздачи | `/plugin-dev:create-plugin` (или точечно `/plugin-dev:plugin-structure`) |

---

**Что бы я сделал дальше** (по фактам, а не наугад): у `founder-post` нет ни `commands/`, ни `agents/`, ни `hooks/` — только скиллы. Самый дешёвый шаг с наибольшим эффектом — добавить одну команду-вход `/post`, чтобы коллеге не нужно было помнить имена четырёх скиллов.

# Skill Development for Claude Code Plugins

This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills for Claude Code plugins.

## About Skills

Skills are modular, self-contained packages that extend Claude's capabilities by providing
specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools. Think of them as "onboarding guides" for specific
domains or tasks—they transform Claude from a general-purpose agent into a specialized agent
equipped with procedural knowledge that no model can fully possess.

### What Skills Provide

1. Specialized workflows - Multi-step procedures for specific domains
2. Tool integrations - Instructions for working with specific file formats or APIs
3. Domain expertise - Company-specific knowledge, schemas, business logic
4. Bundled resources - Scripts, references, and assets for complex and repetitive tasks

### Anatomy of a Skill

Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:

```
skill-name/
├── SKILL.md (required)
│   ├── YAML frontmatter metadata (required)
│   │   ├── name: (required)
│   │   └── description: (required)
│   └── Markdown instructions (required)
└── Bundled Resources (optional)
    ├── scripts/          - Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.)
    ├── references/       - Documentation intended to be loaded into context as needed
    └── assets/           - Files used in output (templates, icons, fonts, etc.)
```

#### SKILL.md (required)

**Metadata Quality:** The `name` and `description` in YAML frontmatter determine when Claude will use the skill. Be specific about what the skill does and when to use it. Use the third-person (e.g. "This skill should be used when..." instead of "Use this skill when...").

#### Bundled Resources (optional)

##### Scripts (`scripts/`)

Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.) for tasks that require deterministic reliability or are repeatedly rewritten.

- **When to include**: When the same code is being rewritten repeatedly or deterministic reliability is needed
- **Example**: `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` for PDF rotation tasks
- **Benefits**: Token efficient, deterministic, may be executed without loading into context
- **Note**: Scripts may still need to be read by Claude for patching or environment-specific adjustments

##### References (`references/`)

Documentation and reference material intended to be loaded as needed into context to inform Claude's process and thinking.

- **When to include**: For documentation that Claude should reference while working
- **Examples**: `references/finance.md` for financial schemas, `references/mnda.md` for company NDA template, `references/policies.md` for company policies, `references/api_docs.md` for API specifications
- **Use cases**: Database schemas, API documentation, domain knowledge, company policies, detailed workflow guides
- **Benefits**: Keeps SKILL.md lean, loaded only when Claude determines it's needed
- **Best practice**: If files are large (>10k words), include grep search patterns in SKILL.md
- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.

##### Assets (`assets/`)

Files not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output Claude produces.

- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output
- **Examples**: `assets/logo.png` for brand assets, `assets/slides.pptx` for PowerPoint templates, `assets/frontend-template/` for HTML/React boilerplate, `assets/font.ttf` for typography
- **Use cases**: Templates, images, icons, boilerplate code, fonts, sample documents that get copied or modified
- **Benefits**: Separates output resources from documentation, enables Claude to use files without loading them into context

### Progressive Disclosure Design Principle

Skills use a three-level loading system to manage context efficiently:

1. **Metadata (name + description)** - Always in context (~100 words)
2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)
3. **Bundled resources** - As needed by Claude (Unlimited*)

*Unlimited because scripts can be executed without reading into context window.

## Skill Creation Process

To create a skill, follow the "Skill Creation Process" in order, skipping steps only if there is a clear reason why they are not applicable.

### Step 1: Understanding the Skill with Concrete Examples

Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.

To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.

### Where skills live

Where you store a skill determines who can use it:

| Location   | Path                                                | Applies to                     |
| :--------- | :-------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------- |
| Enterprise | See [managed settings](/docs/en/settings#settings-files) | All users in your organization |
| Personal   | `~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`            | All your projects              |
| Project    | `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`              | This project only              |
| Plugin     | `<plugin>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`             | Where plugin is enabled        |

When skills share the same name across levels, enterprise overrides personal, and personal overrides project. A skill at any of these levels also overrides a bundled skill with the same name. For example, a `code-review` skill in your project's `.claude/skills/` replaces the bundled `/code-review`. Plugin skills use a `plugin-name:skill-name` namespace, so they cannot conflict with other levels. If you have files in `.claude/commands/`, those work the same way, but if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence.

Skills also load from nested `.claude/skills/` directories below your working directory. When Claude reads or edits a file in a subdirectory, skills from that subdirectory's `.claude/skills/` become available. This lets a monorepo package provide its own skills that apply when working on that package, even if the session started at the repo root.

If a nested skill shares a name with another skill, both stay available. For example, with a `deploy` skill at the project root and another in `apps/web/.claude/skills/`:

* The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`.
* Its description says which directory it applies to.
* Claude picks the variant that matches the files it is working on.

Typing `/deploy` runs the project-root skill. Type the qualified name `/apps/web:deploy` to run the nested variant explicitly.

When you or Claude invoke the unqualified name, the project-root skill loads, and Claude Code appends a list of the directory-qualified variants to its content with an instruction to also invoke any variant whose directory holds the files Claude is working on. A nested skill therefore still applies to work in its directory when only the unqualified name is invoked. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later.

A `<skill-name>` entry in the enterprise, personal, or project locations can be a symlink to a directory elsewhere on disk. Claude Code follows the symlink and reads `SKILL.md` from the target directory, and if the same target is reachable from more than one location, Claude Code loads the skill once. Plugin skills handle symlinks differently; see [Share files within a marketplace with symlinks](/docs/en/plugins-reference#share-files-within-a-marketplace-with-symlinks).

<Note>
  Add a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to a skill folder and it loads as a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins-reference#skills-directory-plugins) named `<name>@skills-dir`, so it can bundle agents, hooks, and MCP servers. In a project's `.claude/skills/`, this requires accepting the workspace trust dialog first.
</Note>

#### Live change detection

Claude Code watches skill directories for file changes. Adding, editing, or removing a skill under `~/.claude/skills/`, the project `.claude/skills/`, or a `.claude/skills/` inside an `--add-dir` directory takes effect within the current session without restarting. Creating a top-level skills directory that did not exist when the session started requires restarting Claude Code so the new directory can be watched.

<Note>
  Live change detection covers `SKILL.md` text only. For a skill folder that is also a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins-reference#skills-directory-plugins), changes to `hooks/`, `.mcp.json`, `agents/`, and `output-styles/` need `/reload-plugins` to take effect.
</Note>

=== lifecycle (когда применяются изменения) ===
### Skill content lifecycle

When you or Claude invoke a skill, the rendered `SKILL.md` content enters the conversation as a single message and stays there for the rest of the session. This persistence applies to the skill's instructions, not its permissions: an [`allowed-tools`](#pre-approve-tools-for-a-skill) grant clears when you send your next message. Claude Code does not re-read the skill file on later turns, so write guidance that should apply throughout a task as standing instructions rather than one-time steps.

When Claude re-invokes a skill whose rendered content is identical to the copy already in context, Claude Code adds a short note that the skill is already loaded rather than a second copy of the content. When the rendered content differs, because the arguments changed or a [dynamic context](#inject-dynamic-context) command produced new output, Claude Code appends the full content again. Before v2.1.202, every re-invocation appended another full copy of the skill's instructions.

[Auto-compaction](/docs/en/how-claude-code-works#when-context-fills-up) carries invoked skills forward within a token budget. When the conversation is summarized to free context, Claude Code re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill after the summary, keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each. Re-attached skills share a combined budget of 25,000 tokens. Claude Code fills this budget starting from the most recently invoked skill, so older skills can be dropped entirely after compaction if you have invoked many in one session.

If a skill seems to stop influencing behavior after the first response, the content is usually still present and the model is choosing other tools or approaches. Strengthen the skill's `description` and instructions so the model keeps preferring it, or use [hooks](/docs/en/hooks) to enforce behavior deterministically. If the skill is large or you invoked several others after it, re-invoke it after compaction to restore the full content.

### Pre-approve tools for a skill

The `allowed-tools` field grants permission for the listed tools during the turn that invokes the skill, so Claude can use them without prompting you for approval. The grant clears when you send your next message, even though the skill content [stays in context](#skill-content-lifecycle); invoking the skill again re-applies it for that turn. It does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable, and your [permission settings](/docs/en/permissions) still govern tools that are not listed. To pre-approve tools for the whole session rather than a single turn, add allow rules to those permission settings instead.

For skills checked into a project's `.claude/skills/` directory, `allowed-tools` takes effect after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder, the same as permission rules in `.claude/settings.json`. Review project skills before trusting a repository, since a skill can grant itself broad tool access.
